Lūdī et lūdibria · Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

backstroke in Latin

backstroke

natātiō resupīna

Neo-LatinComposed phrasesDraft
  • natātiō resupīna — backstroke modern (Traupman 50; M-O s.v. swimming)
  • natātiō retrōgrada — backstroke modern also used (M-O s.v. swimming)
  • Resupīnus natā, sīcut lutra. — Swim on your back, like an otter. composed1

See also: breaststroke, front crawl, swimming.

  1. Why lutra, not lūtra: Lewis & Short prints a long u but gives no evidence, and its only etymological note, luō, has a short one. De Vaan (2008: 355) prints lutra, from PIE *ud-ro- “of the water”, with the short u of Sanskrit udrá- and Greek ὕδρος; Italian and Portuguese lontra and French loutre continue a short u. Ruling: lutra with a short u
Sources & evidence

Lewis & Short: resupinus · Lewis & Short: retrogradus
